name: Iban
catalog_quote: intonation is regarded as comprising stress, pitch and vowel quantity. These three elements are not phonemic. ... Stress in Iban always falls on the final syllable of a word. Any word receiving emphasis, with or without an emphasizing word (cf. 4.37), is stressed.

audit.recode_to: conflict (final per Asmah 1969:69-70 and Scott 1957:509 [isolation forms only, 'slightly'] vs. penultimate-unless-schwa per Howell & Bailey 1900:viii, Richards 1981:xiv-xv, Adelaar 1992:23); if the catalog must carry one word-level pattern, weight-hedged Malay-type (penult; schwa penult -> final; schwa+NC/rC penult keeps stress) like stan1306, keeping domain LUMPED and a 'final prominence = citation-form/phrase-final marker' caveat (Blust 2013:186, 253). Either way add contra = Richards 1981:xiv-xv, Howell & Bailey 1900:viii, Adelaar 1992:23; add Scott 1957:509 as confirming for isolation forms.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim in the held Asmah Haji Omar 1969 SOAS thesis, §2.6 'Intonation', PDF pp. 71-72 ( lines 3116-3133). sources.quote: p. 69 (section 2.6 Intonation): "For the purpose of this thesis, intonation is regarded as comprising stress, pitch and vowel quantity. These three elements are not phonemic. The stress is considered as the primary intonation element, as a heavy stress is usually accompanied by a high pitch and a longer duration of the vowel which forms the nucleus of the stressed syllable." p. 70: "Stress in Iban always falls on the final syllable of a word. sources.quote: 'The following notes on the phonetic interpretation of this spelling are based on the pronunciation of speakers from the Second Division of Sarawak. The descriptions refer to words spoken in isolation, which have slightly increased stress on the final syllable.' Confirms final prominence, but only for citation forms and described as slight -- consistent with the record's LUMPED (word/phrase not separated) caveat.
sources.note: The only phonetician's description of Iban (Asmah 1969 herself calls it the sole modern phonetic treatment); p.509 extract confirms 'slightly increased stress on the final syllable' in isolation words; full 4 pp. needed to see whether he qualifies this (schwa penults, phrase context) and to cite it as an independent confirming source.

sources.quote: 'Stress falls on the penultimate syllable, unless this contains a schwa, in which case it falls on the last syllable. It is not phonemic, nor are there any other phonemically relevant suprasegmental features.' fn.56: 'cf. Richards (1981:XIV-XV), who furthermore specifies that stress falls on the last syllable if the penultimate vowel is a schwa, unless this schwa is followed by a consonant cluster containing r + a consonant, or a homorganic nasal + stop.'
